title: Initial-load validation misses an invalid same-document transition

scenario.observed_change: A UI rejects an invalid selection fragment during a fresh document load, but after the app is already mounted the same invalid fragment only updates status text while leaving the previous successful result visible and does not restore coherent state after a later valid transition.
controlled_inputs: sequence of invalid then valid selection state
authority_boundaries: initial validation path versus post-mount transition path
visible prior result versus current invalid selection state
operation_model: mount successfully with a valid selection
change the same document to an invalid application-owned fragment
handler changes only status while retaining stale successful output
change back to a valid fragment and observe incoherent recovery state

required_invariants.requirement: Stateful lifecycle changes must test materially reachable post-mount transitions and recovery, not only equivalent inputs on initial load.

must_investigate: whether invalid state after mount follows the same fail-closed invariant as initial mount
whether a later valid transition clears stale error state and restores a coherent result
must_identify: fresh-document coverage does not establish correctness of the same-document transition path
must_not_claim: fail-closed selection handling solely from initial-load invalid-input tests
coherent recovery when stale successful content can remain visible under an invalid current state

provenance.note: Codex found that invalid Playground-owned fragments after mount did not clear the prior result or shared context, while the existing browser test forced a fresh document and missed that transition.
